skill.description: Reference guide for implementing Prisma ORM v7 driver adapters. Covers interface contracts, transaction lifecycles, value conversion, error mapping, database notes, and verification.
skill.summary: Guide Prisma v7 driver adapter contracts, transaction lifecycles, value mapping, error handling, and verification.

security_audit.summary: All 69 static alerts are false positives from Markdown, TypeScript examples, expected byte decoding, and a standard DATABASE_URL reference. A separate high-severity data-integrity issue exists because connectToShadowDb() can reuse the primary database URL.

remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit shadowDatabaseUrl or create an isolated temporary database. Never fall back to the primary connection URL in connectToShadowDb().

static_findings.snippet: **Critical**: `commit()` and `rollback()` are **lifecycle hooks only**. They must NOT issue SQL. Pri
Map driver errors to `MappedError` for Prisma to handle correctly:
- Set `safeIntegers: true` when opening the database to get `bigint` for large integers
- `executeScript`: split on `;` and run each statement individually
- Transactions require a dedicated connection (`reserve()` pattern)
- `executeScript`: use multi-statement execution (`.simple()` in some drivers)
- `int8` columns may return as string (already stringified by driver)
- `numeric` columns return as string to preserve precision
- Handle `BIGINT` as string for large values
- [ ] `commit()` and `rollback()` are lifecycle hooks only (no SQL issued)
- [ ] Errors wrapped in `DriverAdapterError` with proper `MappedError` kind
- All standard isolation levels are valid

semantic_findings.title: Primary Database Reused as Shadow Database
semantic_findings.description: connectToShadowDb() falls back to the primary connection URL when no shadow URL is supplied. Migration shadow operations could alter or erase primary data.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The fallback is explicit in the example, and shadow databases are isolated migration workspaces. Reusing the primary URL creates a direct data-integrity hazard.

content.value_statement: Prisma driver adapters require precise transaction, type, and error contracts. This guide provides implementation patterns and verification steps for Prisma ORM v7 adapters.
actual_capabilities: Defines the Prisma v7 factory, adapter, queryable, transaction, query, and result interfaces.
Explains transaction lifecycle hooks, isolation validation, nested savepoints, and resource release.
Provides patterns for argument conversion, row conversion, and column type inference.
Shows database error conversion into Prisma DriverAdapterError and MappedError values.
Supplies unit, end-to-end, and implementation checklists for adapter verification.
limitations: The examples are illustrative and require adaptation to each database driver API.
The skill does not provide a complete package, build configuration, or dependency setup.
End-to-end verification requires a real database, generated Prisma client, and test isolation.
The factory example must not reuse the primary URL for shadow database connections.

use_cases.title: Build a New Adapter
use_cases.description: Implement the required Prisma v7 contracts for a database driver and map its native types and errors.

use_cases.title: Upgrade an Existing Adapter
use_cases.description: Compare an older adapter with Prisma v7 transaction, factory, query, and result requirements.

use_cases.title: Review Adapter Correctness
use_cases.description: Check lifecycle behavior, type conversion, error mapping, disposal, and integration tests before release.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Contracts
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the Prisma v7 SqlDriverAdapter interfaces for a developer new to adapters. Include each required method and its return type.

prompt_templates.title: Design Query Mapping
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my driver API and design queryRaw and executeRaw mappings. Preserve parameter binding and map results to SqlResultSet.

prompt_templates.title: Implement Transactions
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement transaction support for [database]. Validate supported isolation levels, handle nested savepoints, release resources, and keep lifecycle hooks free of SQL.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Complete Adapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Prisma v7 adapter against the guide. Identify contract violations in transactions, type conversion, error mapping, disposal, shadow databases, and tests.

output_examples.input: Explain which interfaces a PostgreSQL Prisma v7 adapter must implement.
output: Factory: connects to primary and isolated shadow databases.
Adapter: executes queries and scripts, starts transactions, reports connection information, and disposes resources.
Transaction: supports queries while commit and rollback only release resources.
Finding: commit sends SQL although Prisma already sends the transaction command.
Fix: keep commit as a lifecycle hook that releases the reserved connection.
Test: verify commit, rollback, nested savepoints, and isolation validation.

output_examples.input: Create a verification plan for a SQLite adapter.
output: Verify integer, bytes, date, JSON, and boolean conversions.
Reject unsupported isolation levels and test script execution behavior.
Run direct adapter tests and end-to-end PrismaClient CRUD and rollback tests.

best_practices: Bind query arguments through the driver instead of interpolating application values into SQL.
Reserve a dedicated connection for transactions and release it through lifecycle hooks.
Use an isolated shadow database and test every supported database behavior with PrismaClient.
anti_patterns: Do not issue COMMIT or ROLLBACK SQL from transaction lifecycle hooks.
Do not infer all database types from JavaScript values when driver metadata is available.
Do not connect shadow database operations to the primary database URL.

faq.question: Which Prisma version does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers Prisma ORM v7 driver adapter interfaces and lifecycle expectations.

faq.question: Does this skill provide a complete adapter package?
faq.answer: No. It provides reference interfaces, implementation patterns, database notes, and verification guidance.

faq.question: Why must commit and rollback avoid issuing SQL?
faq.answer: Prisma sends transaction SQL through executeRaw. These methods should only finalize adapter resources.

faq.question: Which databases are discussed?
faq.answer: The guide includes notes for SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, and MariaDB, plus provider support for SQL Server.

faq.question: How should byte values be handled?
faq.answer: Convert Prisma base64 strings into the driver byte type and return byte results in Prisma-compatible form.

faq.question: What testing is required?
faq.answer: Use direct adapter tests and PrismaClient end-to-end tests for queries, scripts, transactions, conversions, errors, and disposal.
